name: SWCompression
baseline: Compression framework COMPRESSION_ZLIB / NSData.compressed(using: .zlib), and Apple's LZ4
verdict_reason: Its own benchmarks on an M4 MacBook Air show Deflate decompression at about 13.5 MB/s and LZ4 decompression at 52-70 MB/s. Stock zlib decompresses at 314 MB/s and LZ4 at 3832 MB/s on a server core, so the pure-Swift codecs are one to two orders of magnitude slower than the C ones they would replace.
tier_reason: The project's own benchmark command with hardware, macOS and Swift versions stated; the comparison to zlib and LZ4 is across sources and machines.
claimed_speedup: Slower, not faster: Deflate (gzip) decompress 13.4-13.6 MB/s vs 314 MB/s for zlib -6 (about 23x slower); LZ4 decompress 51.8-70.3 MB/s vs 3832 MB/s for lz4 (55-74x slower) (derived across two pages and two machines)
workload: Decompress three real data sets (Git 2.15.0 source, the VS Code 1.18.1 app, Linux 4.14.2 documentation), averaged over 10 iterations, release build
platforms: iOS 18+, macOS 15+, tvOS 18+, watchOS 11+, visionOS 2+, Linux, Windows
install: Swift Package Manager (CocoaPods and Carthage only up to 4.8.6)
one_liner: Pure-Swift decompressors for Deflate, LZ4, LZMA, BZip2 and archive formats; roughly 23-74x slower than the C codecs.
how_it_is_fast: It is not fast. Every codec is implemented in Swift on top of a bit reader (BitByteData) with bounds-checked array access, and none uses the hand-tuned C or SIMD decoders that zlib, LZ4 or Apple's Compression framework use. Its value is format coverage and portability, not speed.
use_it_when: Formats the Compression framework does not read: BZip2, 7-Zip, TAR, XZ containers on Linux
Pure-Swift builds on Linux or Windows with no C dependencies
skip_it_when: Deflate, LZ4 or LZMA decoding on Apple platforms, where the Compression framework is built in and far faster
Large archives or hot paths where decode time shows up
caveats: The zlib and LZ4 reference speeds come from lzbench on an AMD EPYC server core, not the M4; an M4 core is likely faster than that server core at 3.2 GHz, so the real gap on the same machine is probably larger
Compression-speed rows are not comparable across sources because the ratios differ, so only decompression is compared
Data sets differ: SWCompression's three sets versus lzbench's Silesia corpus
tradeoffs: Much lower throughput than C codecs
Deflate compression ratio is weaker than zlib's, per the project's own to-do list

evidence.quote: In this document you can find the results of benchmarking which was performed on Macbook Air M4, 15-inch, 2025.
All tests were run using swcomp's "benchmark" command. SWCompression (and swcomp) were compiled using "Release" configuration.
